_what: The M11 soak window (#389, O5, SDS §12.6). Written when the clock started.
_why_committed: A window-start epoch held only on the Pi is one SD-card failure from making thirty days ungradeable. This file is the durable record; the same numbers are on issue #389.
host: AVID — Raspberry Pi 4 Model B Rev 1.5, 2 GB

_restarted_once.why_restarted: Deliberately, ~28 minutes in, to test that the soak survives a reboot — and to land the intervention log (#389/S12.6) before the real window rather than during it. Discovering on day 29 that a power blip invalidates the record is the disaster this milestone is arranged to avoid; discovering it 28 minutes in costs 28 minutes.
_restarted_once.result: Pi rebooted unattended and came back: robot active, soak-sampler active, samples.db persisted across the reboot and the sampler resumed writing to the same file.

_grade_command_cwd: The leading `cd` is load-bearing. [ai] personality is a RELATIVE path and SDS §6.5 resolves relative paths against the process working directory, which for robot.service is WorkingDirectory=/opt/avid. The command recorded here from 2026-08-22 until 2026-08-23 omitted it and raised FileNotFoundError before grading a single criterion.

_first_grade_pass.AC_3b_unplanned_stops: 1 - FAIL. Boot c7c6c3d5 last seen 1787406043, 22.5 minutes into the window, stopped_at NULL.
_first_grade_pass._does_this_end_the_window: NO, and the reasoning is on the record so it is not re-litigated on day 29. O5 is '30-day soak, >=99% uptime, zero manual restarts' and SDS §12.6 defines an unclean stop as NOT manual: 'an unclean stop is a crash or watchdog kill and is not manual - but it is a defect, counted and reported separately.' Both of O5's own bars pass. §12.6 also says 'zero is the expectation; any occurrence is a finding with its own issue', which is what AC-3b is for - so this is filed, not absorbed, and the window keeps running.
_first_grade_pass._but_note_the_exit_code: AC-3b failing makes the harness exit non-zero. A future operator must not read that exit code as 'O5 failed'. Read the per-criterion lines.

_unplanned_stop_2026_08_22.issue: #439 - filed per SDS §12.6, 'zero is the expectation; any occurrence is a finding with its own issue'.
_unplanned_stop_2026_08_22.what: The MACHINE rebooted about 22.5 minutes into the window. Robot boot c7c6c3d5 - the very boot named in boot_id_at_open above - died with stopped_at NULL; b566ffd9 came up 24s later and has run since.
_unplanned_stop_2026_08_22.not_the_deliberate_reboot: The deliberate reboot under _restarted_once is a DIFFERENT and EARLIER event: boots 5e1009ea and e5e1d1ee stopped at 13:15:21 and 13:16:06 with stop_reason=signal, i.e. cleanly. The graceful path demonstrably records a signal on this machine, so the 13:40:43 stop was not graceful.
evidence_it_was_a_machine_reboot: journald holds nothing before 13:40:53 - the previous boot's log is gone
robot.service and soak-sampler.service both ActiveEnter 13:40:53 / 13:41:13, NRestarts=0
boot_log.started_mono for b566ffd9 is 48.7s - a fresh boot - against 15726s for e5e1d1ee
systemd-timesyncd stepped the clock 13:17:20 -> 13:40:47 'restoring from recorded timestamp', and the kernel's first entry this boot is stamped 2026-04-27 19:48:59
_unplanned_stop_2026_08_22.cause: A HARD POWER LOSS OR HARDWARE RESET. Established by elimination on 2026-08-23, not observed. /var/log/wtmp persists across reboots (journald here does not) and has NO 'shutdown system down' record for this boot, while every other reboot in the machine's history has one - so no software shutdown path ran. Every remaining software route is independently excluded: kernel.panic=0 and panic_on_oops=0, so a panic HANGS this board rather than rebooting it; RuntimeWatchdogUSec=0, so the systemd hardware watchdog is disabled; robot.service has WatchdogUSec=30s and Restart=always but NRestarts=0, so its watchdog never fired (and it restarts a unit, it cannot reboot a machine); OOMPolicy=stop and RSS was flat at 234.0 MiB with 1524 MiB available; the nearest timer is systemd-tmpfiles-clean 17 minutes later and dpkg.log has no activity that day. Corroborated by 'EXT4-fs: orphan cleanup' on mount.
_unplanned_stop_2026_08_22.clock_warning: This Pi has no RTC, and the soak's own evidence table proves the consequence. Ordered by ROWID (write order) rather than by `at`, row 24 was written BEFORE row 25 and is stamped one second LATER: 13:41:08 then 13:41:07. Row 24 carries uptime_s=1492 - exactly 1432+60, the OLD process still alive and counting - and row 25 is the new boot's first sample. Rows 23-24 are in the pre-reboot clock frame and rows 25+ in the post-reboot frame, and the two are not the same timeline: the new boot came up reading 2026-04-27, was set to 13:17:08 by fake-hwclock, stepped again to 13:40:47 by timesyncd 'restoring from recorded timestamp', and only reached true time when NTP landed at 13:44:12 after repeated timeouts. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE: AC-0's '209s gap' and AC-2's '78s down' are subtractions ACROSS TWO CLOCKS, not measurements. Anchoring on monotonic evidence puts the kernel boot at true ~13:40:18, EARLIER than the old system's last sample, so the pre-reboot clock was running at least ~50s ahead of true. This does not move O5 - tens of seconds against a 7h12m budget - but the harness reports these as measurements and they are not. See #439 AC-4. boot_log.started_mono is the column that survives a reboot; this is AVID-345.
_unplanned_stop_2026_08_22.robot_was_healthy_at_the_instant: Nothing degraded first. Across the last six samples RSS held 234.0 MiB to 0.1 MiB, mem_available ~1524 MiB, every bus queue dropped:0, /health answering. Instantaneous is what a power loss looks like and what almost nothing else does.
_unplanned_stop_2026_08_22.why_power_was_lost: STILL UNKNOWN, and it may stay that way. Hypothesis worth eliminating before #400: #413 landed the same day and 2026-08-22 is the FIRST day the robot drove servos under its own service, so the servo rail is a plausible brownout source. That is a hypothesis, not a finding.

_second_occurrence_policy.decided: 2026-08-23, BEFORE a second one occurred (#439 AC-5).
_second_occurrence_policy.rule: A second unplanned stop does NOT end or restart this window. AC-3b keeps reporting the count and each occurrence is a finding with its own issue (SDS §12.6).
_second_occurrence_policy.why: O5's bars are >=99% uptime and zero MANUAL restarts, and §12.6 defines an unclean stop as not manual. Ending a window on a criterion O5 does not contain would be inventing a bar mid-run - and in the flattering direction, since a restarted window is one whose failures have been discarded.
_second_occurrence_policy.but_it_is_not_free: Permitted downtime is 7h12m across the WHOLE thirty days, and RUNBOOK §4.0 is right that the costs are cumulative and unrecoverable. Each stop spends uptime and AC-0 coverage. A handful of them fails this window on AC-2 - honestly, on a bar agreed in advance, which is the only kind of failure worth having.
_second_occurrence_policy.what_WOULD_restart_the_window: A deploy. That is the only restart trigger anywhere in this repo (§12.6's split-window rule), it is an explicit operator decision, and it must be recorded here rather than absorbed. Reliability events are reported; build changes invalidate.
_second_occurrence_policy._decided_in_advance_on_purpose: Deciding this after a second stop is how a window gets quietly restarted to make a number look better. The reasoning is committed so day 29 inherits it rather than re-litigating it under pressure.
